title: Find your way through the work.
intro: Start with the person who needs the thing. Follow the question into a choice, a first version and something they can use. Pick up the part you need today, and come back when the work sends you somewhere else.

stages.title: Figure it out
stages.question: Who is this for, and what do we need to learn?
stages.description: Look at the situation before settling on an answer. Find the consequential question, follow the sources and make the assumptions visible.
stages.output: A question worth investigating, the evidence behind it and the gaps still open.
stages.reflection: New information can change the question. Come back when an assumption stops holding.

stages.title: Make a call
stages.question: What is worth making, for whom, and in what form?
stages.description: Put the options and tradeoffs where you can see them. Choose a direction, a shape that fits and a next step you can explain.
stages.output: One clear choice, its reasons and the next test or plan.
stages.reflection: If the options all feel wrong, go back to the person and the question before choosing again.

stages.title: Build something
stages.question: What is the first version we can put in front of someone?
stages.description: Turn the plan into parts with clear responsibilities. Choose the building guide and tools that fit, then make their behavior and limits inspectable.
stages.output: A first version with clear responsibilities, boundaries and checks.
stages.reflection: What you discover while building may change the plan. Bring that evidence back into the next choice.

stages.title: Make it better
stages.question: Where does the experience get in someone’s way?
stages.description: Look at the experience, the design and the parts that failed. Make a deliberate revision and name the evidence that would show it helped.
stages.output: One intentional improvement and a way to check its usefulness.
stages.reflection: A new observation may call for a small revision, another prototype or a different direction.

stages.title: Make it visible
stages.question: How can someone see what this is and why it matters?
stages.description: Find the visual direction, tell the story and show the real product. Bring images, films and demonstrations through review with their purpose still clear.
stages.output: A visual direction, image, film or product demonstration ready for review.
stages.reflection: If the story is hard to tell, revisit who the work serves and the choice you made.

stages.title: Take it somewhere new
stages.question: What needs to carry over when the setting changes?
stages.description: Move an application into another language, bring a capability to another host or plan its release. Make the behavior to preserve and the checks for that move explicit.
stages.output: A move or release plan, with checks for what must carry over.
stages.reflection: A move can reveal a new constraint. Return to the choice, build or improvement that needs another look.

stages.title: Pick it up again
stages.question: What will the next person need to keep this going?
stages.description: Keep the source record, explain the current state and leave a useful next step. Bring the right people in with the context and access they need.
stages.output: An inspectable record, clear ownership and a place for someone to begin.
stages.reflection: The next person may be you next week. What they find can become the beginning of another question.
